attempted_claim: Fix small delta>0. Let q be q^delta-smooth (not assumed squarefree), let chi be a primitive Dirichlet character modulo q, and let S(M,N)=sum_{M<n<=M+N} chi(n) with 1<=N<=q. Prove unconditionally, uniformly in M, S(M,N) <<_epsilon N^{23/41} q^{11/82+O(delta)+epsilon} for every epsilon>0, with absolute implied O(delta), and hence L(1/2,chi) <<_epsilon q^{27/164+O(delta)+epsilon}. In particular, does Irving's A^3B exponent pair (11/82,57/82) for short sums at N approx sqrt(q) extend from squarefree smooth q to general smooth q?
decisive_failure: The target bound was not proved: closing the gap needs a uniform prime-power p-adic replacement for Irving's B-step plus degenerate-shift counting, a multi-week program beyond this pass. The bounded computation covers only small moduli (q<=49 broadly, q=49/169 focused) and low-degree shift families, so it characterizes the obstruction point rather than substituting for the missing theory. No fallback or emergent submission is made.
